week_notes: Side leans 2-10, total leans 4-8, the worst week of the season so far. On the merits: sides 2-6 with 4 decided by chance (NYJ_NE, PIT_TB, BUF_LV, WAS_SF), totals 3-5 with 4 decided by chance (garbage time in CHI_ATL and NO_NYG, overtime in PIT_TB, a return or defensive touchdown in TEN_IND).
Average miss on the margin: model 8.38, market 6.58; on the total: model 10.31, market 9.33. The market beat the model on both.

Biggest margin misses: TEN @ IND (14.9), ARI @ LA (14.1), CAR @ PHI (11.7), BAL @ CLE (10.6). Two of them came with a starting quarterback out (Hurts for PHI; Huntley throwing for BAL), where the board's number had moved and the model's raw number had not, the same pattern seen again in week 11 (IND_HOU, ARI_KC).

Several quarterbacks who played were not projected at all (Huntley, Caleb Williams in his return), so their teams' pass catchers were projected off the wrong passer. A data check on the starting-QB input for week 6 is worth doing before any test reads this week's player misses.
Staked bets went 0-2; the rest are the model's leans, not money.

2026_06_BAL_CLE.headline: CLE won 13-10 on a field goal at 0:00 after BAL led 10-0 after the first quarter. Both leans lost on the merits. The model had BAL by 7.6 and 44 points, but Tyler Huntley, not Lamar Jackson, threw BAL's passes.
right: The board's number (BAL by 3.7, total 39.6) stayed close to the market; the leans came from the model's own number, which was further off.
wrong: Side lean BAL -3 (model BAL by 7.6) lost: CLE by 3. The model missed by 10.6, the market by 6.
Over 39.5 (model 44.1) lost: 23 points. Both teams punted 7 times on 11 drives: BAL 0.91 points a drive, CLE 1.18. Each missed a field goal. BAL scored 10 in the first quarter and nothing after.

BAL's offense ran at 33% success with 3 explosive plays. Huntley had 193 yards (165 passing, 28 rushing) and wasn't projected. The Yardbarker headline 'Tyler Huntley's missed opportunities proved costly against Browns' points the same way.
The cover was settled late: CLE's touchdown at 8:37 of the fourth made it 10-9, and Andre Szmyt's field goal at 0:00 won it (Browns.com, 'Andre Szmyt makes game-winning field goal').
chance: Little luck either way: no defensive or return scores, no short missed field goals, fumble bounces even. BAL fumbled twice and lost one.
A last-play field goal decided the winner, but BAL -3 had already lost once CLE tied it at 10-10.
improve: Candidate data check: the facts list Lamar Jackson as BAL's quarterback, yet Huntley threw the passes. If the model's number assumed Jackson, that would explain most of its 4.6-point gap to the market. Check how the model handles a late starting-QB change.
Possibility: a division game with a low total (39.5). Familiar defenses may have kept both offenses quiet.

Possibility: CLE's Jaleel McLaughlin played 62% of snaps (usually 11%), and Browns.com says Audric Estime scored the tying touchdown in his first week with the team. CLE leaned on new or little-used backs and still won.
Possibility: Tylan Wallace (WR, CLE) faced BAL, his team in 2023-2025.

2026_06_CAR_PHI.headline: CAR beat an injury-hit PHI 25-14 with Tanner McKee starting for the absent Jalen Hurts. The PHI +3 lean lost on the merits; the over missed by half a point.
right: The total was nearly right: 39 points against a 39.5 line and a 40.2 model.
wrong: Side lean PHI +3 (model PHI by 0.7) lost: CAR by 11. The model missed by 11.7, the market by 8; the board (CAR by 2.5) was near the market.

PHI played without Jalen Hurts (Out), both centers who usually play (Cam Jurgens; Drew Kendall, Questionable) and LB Jalyx Hunt (Out). McKee played every snap. PHI had 0 explosive plays and punted 8 times on 11 drives (1.27 points a drive).
CAR ran 77 plays to PHI's 64 and scored 3 touchdowns in 4 red-zone trips. Bryce Young had 289 yards (281 passing), Chuba Hubbard 120 rushing; neither was projected.

The cover was settled early: CAR's field goal at 11:37 of the third made it 13-7, and CAR never trailed. The AP called PHI 'injury-riddled' (via WBTV), and theScore had it as PHI's fourth straight loss.
chance: Not much: no early exits, no return or defensive scores. Fumble bounces gave PHI about 1.6 points (PHI fumbled once and kept it), so luck slightly helped the lean and it still lost.
The over lost by 0.5 on a CAR touchdown with 6:39 left that came with no garbage time. That is close, but not luck by the review's definition.
improve: Candidate data check: the model had PHI by 0.7 with Hurts out, while the board moved to the market. Check whether the model's own number takes in a starting quarterback's absence (same question as BAL_CLE this week).
Possibility: CAR came off 14 days' rest against PHI's 7. A rest edge test is a pre-set question, not a conclusion.
Possibility: Jaelan Phillips (LB) and John Metchie III (WR) faced PHI, their 2025 team. CAR's Taylor Moton played every snap after not playing before.

2026_06_CHI_ATL.headline: CHI led 31-7 entering the fourth quarter in Caleb Williams' return. The ATL +1.5 lean lost on the merits; the under lost only because of 11 garbage-time points.
right: The game script for the total: it sat at 35 points after three quarters and would have stayed under without the garbage-time scoring.
wrong: Side lean ATL +1.5 (model even) lost: CHI by 8. CHI ran 76 plays at 0.149 EPA and 52.5% success; ATL ran 55 at -0.246 and 33%.
ATL turned it over on downs 3 times and lost 2 fumbles. CHI scored on 5 of 14 drives (2.21 a drive).

Caleb Williams had 309 yards and wasn't projected. The AP (via AJC) says he completed his first 12 passes in his return after missing 3 games. Luther Burden III had 95 receiving yards, also unprojected.
On the total the market was much closer (missed by 1.5 against 6.5): the model's 47.5 looked too low for a full-strength CHI offense.
chance: Garbage time decided the total: CHI's field goal to start the fourth (31-7) and ATL's touchdown and two-point try at 9:39 came with CHI up 17+, 11 points in all. Without them the game ends 43, under 52.5.
Fumble luck was even: each team fumbled 3 times and lost 2. No return or defensive scores.
improve: Possibility: CHI's rating may have leaned on the 3 games without Williams. Worth a data check on how the model weights games a starting quarterback missed when he returns.
Possibility: Kyler Gordon (CB, CHI) had 3 sacks and 2 forced fumbles, even with CHI missing Montez Sweat, T.J. Edwards (Out) and Xavier Woods.
Possibility: five players faced a former team, including Grady Jarrett (CHI, ATL 2023-2024) and Gervon Dexter Sr. (ATL, CHI 2023-2025).

2026_06_NO_NYG.headline: NO scored 34 straight points and won 34-27 after NYG led 10-0. The NYG +1.5 lean lost on the merits; the under lost only to 15 garbage-time points.
right: Through 34-10 the total read was on track: 44 points with 11:31 left, under 46.5.
wrong: Side lean NYG +1.5 (model NYG by 1.7) lost: NO by 7. The model missed by 8.7, the market by 5.5.
NYG threw 3 interceptions (Martin Emerson 2, Julian Blackmon 1) and lost a fumble. Emerson played 78% of snaps, usually 11%. NYG went 2 of 5 in the red zone.
The cover was settled early: NO's touchdown at 12:31 of the third made it 16-10, the start of 34 straight NO points (AP via ABC News).

Two NYG quarterbacks threw: Jameis Winston 152 passing yards and J.J. McCarthy 243. Malik Nabers had 165 receiving yards on 12 catches; none of them was projected. The facts don't say why NYG changed quarterbacks.
chance: Garbage time decided the total: NO's touchdown at 34-10 and NYG's touchdown and two-point try at 34-18 came with a team up 17+ in the fourth, 15 points. Without them the total is 46, under 46.5 by half a point.
NYG's 17 fourth-quarter points made the final look closer than the game; the side was lost long before.
improve: Possibility: NYG were without RB Cam Skattebo and OL Jermaine Eluemunor (Questionable); Marcus Mbow played every snap (usually 13%).
Possibility: Jameis Winston faced NO, his 2023 team.
Candidate data check: when a team uses two quarterbacks, check which one the model's number assumed.

2026_06_NYJ_NE.headline: NE won 26-19, half a point short of the 7.5 line, after NYJ's field goal with 36 seconds left. Fumble luck against NE flipped the side; the under lost on that same late kick.
right: The model and market both had the shape right: NE by 9.4 and 7.5, NE by 7. The model missed by 2.4, the market by 0.5.
Drake Maye had 260 yards (235 passing); the AP credits him with 3 touchdown passes (via ABC News).
wrong: Under 43.5 (model 42.6) lost: 45 points. It went over only on NYJ's field goal at 0:36 (19-26). NYJ kicked 4 field goals and went 0 of 3 in the red zone.
NYJ turned it over on downs twice and punted only twice; Geno Smith threw for 252 and Braelon Allen had 104 scrimmage yards, none projected.
chance: NE fumbled 3 times and lost 2; NYJ didn't fumble. That cost NE about 1.6 points. With even bounces NE wins by about 8.6 and covers 7.5, so luck flipped the side.
The late NYJ field goal decided both the cover and the total. It was not garbage time (a 10-point game), but it was the last snap that mattered.
improve: Possibility: NYJ's Omar Cooper Jr. played 82% of snaps (usually 7%) and had 103 receiving yards.
Possibility: a division game. NE was without CB Carlton Davis and WR Romeo Doubs; Matt Pryor played 68% on the line (usually 0%).
Possibility: Leonard Taylor III (DT, NE) faced NYJ, his 2024-2025 team.

2026_06_PIT_TB.headline: Regulation ended 19-19; PIT won 26-19 on an overtime touchdown. TB +2.5 would have covered and the over would have lost at the end of regulation, so overtime decided both leans.
right: The model was closer on the total (missed by 3.9 against 6.5), though the over won only in overtime.
TB led 16-3 after three quarters, closer to the model's TB lean than the final shows.
wrong: The model had TB by 0.5 against the market's PIT by 2.5; PIT's 16 fourth-quarter points and overtime touchdown say PIT were at least as good. The AP: Aaron Rodgers threw 2 late touchdown passes as PIT stormed back (via ABC News).
TB's offense ran 74 plays at -0.208 EPA and 31% success, threw 2 interceptions and kicked 4 field goals. Jalon Daniels had 200 yards (164 passing, 39 rushing), unprojected.
DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard had 11 catches each (93 and 87 yards) against a TB defense missing Antoine Winfield Jr. (Out).
chance: Regulation ended 19-19 (38 points, under 38.5; TB +2.5 covering). PIT's overtime touchdown flipped both. Overtime is close to a coin flip, so neither lean counts for or against the read.
PIT's field goal with 1:23 left and TB's tying field goal with 0:13 left sent it to overtime. No return scores, fumbles even.
improve: Possibility: TB had 10 days' rest to PIT's 7 and still faded late. Roundtable's headline says TB blew a 13-point lead.
Possibility: Jamel Dean (CB, PIT) faced TB, his 2023-2025 team, and had 1 interception and 6 passes defended. Miles Killebrew and Kenny Gainwell (TB) faced PIT.
Possibility: Rodgers said the Tampa field needs a look (The Sun Papers headline). Footing is a thing the model can't see.

2026_06_TEN_IND.headline: TEN came back from 13-0 at halftime to win 26-20. The IND -6.5 lean lost on the merits; the under lost only because of a TEN return or defensive touchdown.
right: On the total the model's number (43) was not far off. The final was 46, and 7 of those points came from a non-offensive TEN touchdown.
wrong: The side lean, IND -6.5 (model IND by 8.9, 2.4 more than the market), lost: TEN won by 6. The model missed the margin by 14.9, the market by 12.5.
IND ran 82 plays to TEN's 45 and still lost. IND turned it over 3 times (2 interceptions, 1 lost fumble) and was stopped on downs twice in 11 drives.
TEN scored all 26 of its points in the second half: 0-0-6-20 by quarter. The cover swung late, on TEN's touchdown at 13:04 of the fourth quarter (12-13).
TEN's pass rush took over: Jeffery Simmons (2 sacks, a forced fumble) and Jermaine Johnson II (2 sacks, 3 QB hits).
chance: TEN scored a return or defensive touchdown, about 6.3 points of margin and 7 on the total. The AP recap headline says TEN used 'special teams plays and defense to rally' (newschannel9.com).
Fumble bounces were worth about 1.6 more for TEN. With even luck the margin is IND by 1.9: still not a cover, so chance did not flip the side.
Without the 7 non-offensive points the total is 39, under 44.5. Chance decided the total.
improve: Possibility: a division game, and TEN's first win of the season (AP). Familiarity may narrow the gap the model expected.
Possibility: IND played without TE Tyler Warren (usually 91% of snaps); Will Mallory played 52% in his place.
Possibility: TEN played without CB Alontae Taylor and S Kevin Winston, and Joshua Williams played every snap in his first game. IND still could not pull away.
Possibility: DE Jacob Martin faced IND, his team in 2023, and had a sack.

2026_06_ARI_LA.headline: ARI won 18-16 on six field goals, the last at the gun. The ARI +12.5 lean won outright; the over 51.5 lost by a mile with 34 points.
right: The side lean, ARI +12.5, won: ARI won by 2. The model's edge was tiny (LA by 12.1, 0.4 off the market), so this was the market's miss as much as the model's (14.1 against 14.5).
ARI ran 72 plays to LA's 58 and kept the ball away from Stafford's offense.
wrong: The total lean, over 51.5 (model 51.8), lost: 34 points. Both the model and the market missed by about 17.5.
ARI reached the red zone 5 times and scored 0 touchdowns: 6 field goals, 1 turnover, 3 punts (1.8 points a drive).
LA scored 1.45 points a drive: 2 touchdowns, 1 field goal, 2 turnovers on downs, 1 lost fumble. Its only touchdowns came at 8:29 of the second quarter and 0:52 of the fourth.
chance: Little luck either way: no defensive or return scores, no early quarterback exit, even fumble bounces.
The winning kick came as time expired, Chad Ryland's sixth field goal (AP, via ksat.com). The side lean won by enough that the last kick didn't matter for the cover.
improve: Possibility: both offensive lines were short. LA played without OL Alaric Jackson (David Quessenberry played every snap) and ARI without OL Paris Johnson. That may have held the total down.
Possibility: LA played without CB Trent McDuffie (Questionable), yet the passing game still didn't push the total up.
Candidate test: whether red-zone touchdown rate regresses strongly to the mean for totals. ARI's 0 of 5 is a one-game fluke as easily as a trait.
Possibility: a division game in a dome; familiarity may slow offenses.

2026_06_BUF_LV.headline: BUF led 33-23 with two minutes left, then a LV touchdown with 1:39 left made it 33-30. The BUF -5.5 lean lost on that backdoor score; the over won with 63.
right: The total lean, over 53.5 (model 53.6), won: 63 points. Both offenses moved: BUF 3.3 points a drive, LV 3.0.
BUF scored on 7 of 10 drives (3 TDs, 4 FGs) and never turned it over. The AP headline: 'Josh Allen ties Jim Kelly's Bills TD pass record' (abc30.com).
wrong: The side lean, BUF -5.5 (model BUF by 6.2), lost by 2.5 points. The edge was only 0.7, so it was close to a coin flip.
LV scored 17 in the fourth quarter after being held to 0 in the third, and tied it 23-23 with 8:07 left.
chance: The cover was settled late: BUF was ahead by 10 after its field goal at 2:00, and LV's touchdown at 1:39 cut it to 3. That backdoor score decided the side, so it is marked chance.
The total was 53 before that same 2:00 field goal, half a point under. The over needed a late kick in a close game; that's normal football, not garbage time, so it stays a win.
improve: Possibility: CB Taron Johnson faced BUF, his team from 2023 to 2025; his old team knew his habits and threw for a record day.
Possibility: LV played without G Jackson Powers-Johnson and still scored 30. The local recap (news3lv.com) says missed opportunities cost LV.
Possibility: BUF was on 6 days' rest and traveled west for a dome game.

2026_06_LAC_KC.headline: KC won 22-6 coming off a bye, so the KC -7.5 lean won with room to spare. The over 41.5 lost badly: LAC scored 0.5 points a drive.
right: The side lean, KC -7.5 (model KC by 9.7), won: KC by 16. The model was closer than the market (6.3 against 8.5).
The cover was settled early, on KC's touchdown at 1:53 of the second quarter (3-15). KC led 19-3 at the half.
KC's pass rush led: George Karlaftis had a sack, 2 passes defended and 3 QB hits.
wrong: The total lean, over 41.5 (model 44.1, 2.6 above the market), lost: 28 points. The model missed by 16.1, the market by 13.5.
LAC had 1 explosive play, a 29% success rate and -0.26 EPA a play. Its 12 drives: 5 punts, 2 turnovers, 2 turnovers on downs, 2 field goals.
KC left points too: 1 touchdown in 4 red-zone trips, a missed field goal, and a turnover on downs. The AP follow-up says KC 'stew over short-yardage failures' (kctv5.com).
chance: LAC lost both its fumbles and KC recovered its own, worth about 4.9 points to KC. With even luck the margin is KC by 11.1, still a cover.
No defensive or return scores and no garbage-time points, so the under was earned.
improve: Possibility: LAC was short on offense: T Rashawn Slater and WR Tre Harris (Out) didn't play, and KeAndre Lambert-Smith played 87% of snaps (usually none). LAC fell to 0-6 (Roundtable).
Possibility: KC had 14 days' rest after a bye. Kenneth Walker ran for both KC touchdowns (AP, abcnews.com).
Candidate test: lower a total when a team's offense loses a starting tackle and a top receiver at once; the model's over lean ignored both.
Possibility: S Alohi Gilman and CB Kristian Fulton faced LAC, their former team, in a division game.

2026_06_DAL_GB.headline: GB led 17-0 at the half and won 23-13. The under 53.5 won easily with 36 points; the DAL +1.5 lean lost on the merits.
right: The total lean, under 53.5 (model 51.1, 2.4 below the market), won: 36 points. The model was closer than the market (15.1 against 17.5).
DAL was scoreless in the first half (Fox 4 recap, fox4news.com) and scored 1.3 points a drive: 2 turnovers, 2 turnovers on downs, 3 punts.
wrong: The side lean, DAL +1.5 (model GB by 1.1), lost: GB by 10. The edge was small (0.4), and both the model (8.9) and the market (8.5) missed by about the same.
DAL had 1 explosive play on 78 plays and -0.19 EPA a play. Two interceptions, by Brandon Cisse and Evan Williams, ended drives.
GB settled for 3 field goals but led all game; the AP headline credits 'Jordan Love, Green Bay's defense' (fox11online.com).
chance: Little luck: no defensive or return scores, no early quarterback exit, fumble bounces close to even (about 1.6 to GB).
DAL's touchdown with 52 seconds left made it 13-23. It didn't change the cover or the total.
improve: Possibility: three DAL players faced GB, their former team (Kenny Clark, Rashan Gary, Tyler Goodson). Clark had a sack. Knowing each other's habits didn't help DAL's offense.
Possibility: DAL had 10 days' rest and played without G T.J. Bass.
Possibility: GB used WR Savion Williams on 53% of snaps in his first game.
Possibility: a Sunday night game outdoors in Green Bay in mid-October.

2026_06_WAS_SF.headline: SF led 23-3 in the third quarter, then WAS scored the last 14 points to lose 23-17. The SF -7.5 lean lost on a late swing; the under won with 40.
right: The total lean, under 51.5 (model 49.7), won: 40 points. The model was closer than the market (9.7 against 11.5).
SF scored 20 points in the first half and 3 after it. WAS scored 1.7 points a drive, with 2 turnovers on downs.
Beat their projections (one line): Jayden Daniels 300 passing (184), Mike Evans 94 (63), Chig Okonkwo 69 (26).
wrong: The side lean, SF -7.5 (model SF by 10.2), lost by 1.5 points. The market was closer than the model (1.5 against 4.2).

Jayden Daniels ran 3 times for 11 yards against 6.2 carries and 40 yards projected. WAS trailed by 9+ on 66% of its plays, so he threw instead (300 yards). His last game was 103 rushing yards; the projection may have been chasing it.
Terry McLaurin had 27 yards on 1 target (5.5 projected). He played 10% of snaps (usually 72%) after a limited week of practice, so this was an early exit, not a usage choice.
chance: WAS recovered its own fumble and SF lost its one, worth about 3.2 points to WAS. With even luck the margin is SF by 9.2, a cover, so chance flipped the side.
The cover was settled by WAS's touchdown with 9:26 left (17-23), the second of two straight WAS touchdowns.
Newsweek reports a key WAS offensive player left the game with an injury; McLaurin's 10% of snaps fits that, but the headline doesn't name him.
improve: Candidate data fix: leave a player out of the week's miss averages when he played under a quarter of his usual snaps, as with McLaurin here.
Candidate test: cut a pass catcher's projection when he was limited in practice all week.
Possibility: SF played without LB Dre Greenlaw and WR Deebo Samuel; WAS's second-half comeback came against a thinner defense.
Possibility: WAS CB Trey Amos played 58% of snaps in his first game.
